messages:
margo: heads up — hit a telemetry blind spot when v1 clients get 429 and auto-fallback to v2. console charts don't show the switch events because our sampling window collapses them. need a quick triage :eyes:
ben: can you repro? any logs or a curl snippet?
margo: minimal repro below, seen in prod trace where client retries immediately and console shows only aggregate 429s, not the route change.
```
# simulate client with explicit v1 header then retry to v2
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "X-Api-Version: 1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/generate
# got 429 + body {"fallback": "v2", "reason": "quota_exceeded"} then client retried to v2
```
hailey: ah — ingestion currently rolls up route_switch counts into a 60s sampling bucket. if the retry happens in the same bucket we only emit a single aggregated counter (429) and drop the immediate switch event. makes sense this would hide the user-visible fallback.
kevin: from a console/ux POV we need both: an immediate per-request event to show the actual switch + the aggregated timeline for trends. can we emit a lightweight event that has minimal PII?
margo: yeah we can emit a short event: {route_from:v1, route_to:v2, fallback_reason:quota, client_hash:sha256(client_id)}. keep it small and TTL it after 7 days.
ash: (cc ash) do we have perf concerns if we leak a new event stream?
ash: sorry, typo — ash.
ash: ash: small event on fallback path should be cheap; the concern is cardinality of client_hash. we should coarse-hash (e.g., first 8 chars) to keep cardinality low.
ash: also recommend emitting a metric counter route_switch_immediate (tagged by fallback_reason) so the backend dashboards can pivot quickly without parsing events.
kevin: perfect — route_switch_immediate + hashed client telemetry will let us show per-request markers in timeline and still keep trend lines. UX: add an optional toggle in the console called "Show fallbacks" default off for high-cardinality orgs.
margo: sounds good. action items: ash to open ingestion PR, hailey to add a short metric route_switch_immediate, kevin to stub console toggle and experiment endpoint.
ash: i'll own rollout/monitoring for the change and add a guardrail: if cardinality spikes > X we'll auto-disable the immediate event stream for that org.
ash: (typo again, i mean ash signing off) :thumbsup:
eng-deploy-bot: deployment scheduled — canary to eng-platform cluster at 2026-04-02T18:00Z.
ash: quick note — we should also add a small log line at the proxy level when fallback triggers so SREs can correlate traces if needed.
ben: i'll add a tiny test to the traffic-sim harness to cover the immediate fallback emission and ensure console shows a marker.
margo: thanks all. ping me on the PRs and let's try to have a canary by EOD tomorrow. :shipit:
